title: Helping Singaporeans Navigate a High-interest Rate Environment
what_it_is: Helping Singaporeans Navigate a High-interest Rate Environment

sections.label: Domestic interest rates rising
sections.summary: Domestic interest rates are likely to rise with global rates, as US policy rates rose 3% in under six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our domestic interest rates are likely to increase further in tandem with global interest rates as rates here are largely market determined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, US policy rates have been raised to fight inflation by a total of 3% in less than six months, as compared to an almost 0% interest rate for the large part of 2009 to 2021.

sections.label: Households adjust borrowing prudently
sections.summary: Households must adjust borrowings and spending, as MAS and MND revised medium-term rate floors for prudent property borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singaporeans and Singaporean households will need to adjust to the new normal and plan their borrowings and expenditures accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Ministry of National Development (MND) have just announced that there will be revisions to the medium-term rate floors, to ensure that households borrow prudently for their property purchases in a higher interest rate environment, from last month onwards.

sections.label: Bank home loan rates rise
sections.summary: Local banks raised home loan rates from 1.15% in late 2021 to about 3.85%, above HDB's 2.6% rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our local banks have raised home loan rates from 1.15% per annum as recently as late 2021 to around 3.85% just earlier today, surpassing the 2.6% applicable to Housing and Development Board (HDB) loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: HDB's statistics show that 6,800 households applied to refinance their HDB loans with bank loans in FY 2020/2021.

sections.label: Enhancing study loan schemes
sections.summary: Study loan schemes could be enhanced by raising the $2,700 income cap and extending the CPF Education Loan Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As commercial interest rates increase and study loans become less affordable, perhaps we could enhance these existing schemes by raising the $2,700 gross monthly per capita income cap for the MOE Study Loan and extend the CPF Education Loan Scheme to cover more courses including part-time accredited diploma or degree courses.

sections.label: Delayed BTO projects
sections.summary: MND announced in May 2022 that 58 Build-To-Order projects were delayed by at least six months that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: MND had announced in May 2022 that 58 Build-To-Order (BTO) projects were delayed by at least six months this year.

sections.label: Extending TBLP support scheme
sections.summary: TBLP extensions show it effectively meets firms' financing needs, and a further extension or replacement is hoped for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The multiple extensions of TBLP, a support measure implemented to help firms with their financing needs during the pandemic, show that it is effective in meeting its purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider a further extension past the current end-date of the scheme on 30 September 2022, or a replacement that is also focused on providing eligible SMEs with affordable interest rates.

sections.label: MAS raises TDSR interest rates
sections.summary: MAS raised the interest rates used to calculate loan repayments under the TDSR by 0.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The MAS has just raised interest rates used to calculate loan repayments under the TDSR by 0.5%.

sections.label: Rising rates and foreign assets
sections.summary: The passage asks whether rising global interest rates and a possible US recession were considered for volatility in foreign asset investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On the borrowing side, the Government would have to incur higher borrowing rates in taking actions to manage banking system liquidity or even for our infrastructure needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the same time, on the investment side, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence has also shared in this Chamber that over the medium term, rising interest rates will also help to raise investment income from our foreign asset holdings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, has the Government also taken into consideration that the rising global interest rate environment and risk of potential US recession that may occur downstream, could cause increased volatility for our investments in foreign asset holdings?

sections.label: Higher average interest rates ahead
sections.summary: Average interest rates over the next five years or more will likely be higher than the last 15-20 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Average interest rates over the next five years or more will likely be higher than what the world had experienced for the last 15-20 years.

sections.label: Higher interest rate floors for loans
sections.summary: MAS, MND and HDB announced measures raising the medium-term interest rate floor for TDSR and MSR, and an interest rate floor for HDB housing loans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MAS, MND and HDB recently announced measures to increase the medium-term interest rate floor used to compute the TDSR and Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR) for property loans by financial institutions and introduced an interest rate floor for computing eligible loan amounts for housing loans granted by HDB.

sections.label: Schemes to improve productivity
sections.summary: The passage states this is the most effective way to improve competitiveness and lists schemes to help firm and worker productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is the most effective way to improve our overall competitiveness and achieve a win-win outcome for both businesses and workers through economic growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: There are many schemes available, including the Productivity Solutions Grant, the Energy Efficiency Grant, SkillsFuture subsidies and the newly introduced $70 million NTUC Company Training Committee Grant to help improve firm and worker productivity, and to build new enterprise and workforce capabilities.

sections.label: NIRC stability amid market volatility
sections.summary: The NIR framework mitigates short-term market volatility on NIRC by smoothening asset bases and using expected long-term real returns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The impact of short-term market volatility on the Net Investment Returns Contribution, or NIRC, is mitigated as our Net Investment Returns (NIR) framework is designed to provide stability in an uncertain investment environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It does so by smoothening out relevant asset bases over the long-term and calculating NIRC based on the expected long-term real rate of return of the investment entities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As such, the NIRC serves as a steady stream of returns to fund our annual expenditure even in periods of market uncertainty.

sections.label: Additional help beyond Government assistance
sections.summary: This passage states the purpose is to give additional help on top of Government assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: — to give them additional help on top of the assistance from Government.

sections.label: Contributions, social cohesion, social compact
sections.summary: This passage states that small contributions make society caring, and mutual trust and social cohesion help face crises and strengthen the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: When each of us contributes a little to help others, it makes our society more caring and warmer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are able to face stormy seas with greater confidence and resilience than many other countries, because of our mutual trust and our social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And we hope that every crisis will further strengthen our social compact and bring us even closer together as one united people.
